sections.Aims and Fit of Module: This Year 1 module is designed to prepare students for the BA International Relations programme. It introduces the development of political science and international relations as academic disciplines through an examination of key concepts. Students will have the opportunity to develop basic conceptual and theoretical understanding of social sciences broadly, with a particular focus on political science and international relations, by analyzing these areas in the context of the emergence of the modern world. The module lays the foundation for essential academic skills, including critical analysis, structured argumentation, and scholarly writing, while developing the language proficiency required to engage effectively with discipline-specific literature and discourse.
sections.Learning outcomes: A. Demonstrate a basic understanding of key concepts and ideas in international relations and political science B. Demonstrate awareness of the different levels of analysis (system, state, and individual) in the study of international relations C. Apply the key concepts of international relations to explore a specific case study D. Operationalise essential study and research skills relevant to international relations and the broader social sciences
sections.Method of teaching and learning: Teaching on the module is by a combination of lectures and seminars. Lectures introduce key concepts and theories in international relations, using real-world examples to demonstrate their application to complex global issues. Seminars build on this foundation through interactive activities including analysis of current news events, structured group discussions, scenario-based exercises, and simplified case studies. These sessions develop students’ ability to apply I nternational Relations concepts confidently while fostering collaborative learning. Throughout the module, students will develop essential academic skills, such as critical analysis, scholarly writing, and effective research, alongside discipline-specific language proficiency, preparing them for assessments and further study in Year 2 and beyond.
